title: The symmetric algebra of a quasi-coherent module: universal property and sections over affine opens
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a commutative ring $R$ and an $R$-module $M$ let $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$ be the symmetric algebra, with $M=\operatorname{Sym}^1_R(M)\to\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$. Then there are a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$, whose underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent, and an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $j_{\mathcal F}:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ such that: (a) for every sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\mathcal B$ and every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal B$ there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras $\tilde u:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)\to\mathcal B$ with $\tilde u\circ j_{\mathcal F}=u$; (b) for every affine open $U\subseteq X$, with $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, the $R$-algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F(U))\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$ extending $j_{\mathcal F,U}$ is an isomorphism. (Consequently, by (a), an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ between quasi-coherent modules induces a unique algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}(v)$ with $\operatorname{Sym}(v)\circ j_{\mathcal F}=j_{\mathcal F'}\circ v$, functorially.)

source.place: Modules, Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior, line 3262: definition of Sym(F) as a quotient of the tensor algebra), Lemma 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra, line 3303: Sym^n F is the sheafification of U -> Sym^n_{O(U)}(F(U))), Lemma 01CL (lemma-whole-tensor-algebra-permanence, line 3461: Sym of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent); Schemes, Section 01LA item (9) (schemes.tex line 4717); used as Sym^*_{O_X} in Properties, Lemmas 05JS, 086N, 0817

proof.text: *Step 1 (the presheaf $\mathcal P$ of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras).* For an open $U\subseteq X$ put $\mathcal P(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U))$ with $\iota_U:\mathcal F(U)\to\mathcal P(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property], a commutative $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra. For opens $V\subseteq U$, $\mathcal P(V)$ is a commutative $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra through the restriction $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal O_X(V)$, and $s\mapsto\iota_V(s|_V)$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear because the restrictions of $\mathcal F$ are semilinear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; let $\rho_{UV}:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal P(V)$ be the unique $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map with $\rho_{UV}(\iota_U(s))=\iota_V(s|_V)$. By the uniqueness clause, $\rho_{UU}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\rho_{VW}\rho_{UV}=\rho_{UW}$ for $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ (both sides are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra maps sending $\iota_U(s)$ to $\iota_W(s|_W)$). So $\mathcal P$ is a presheaf of commutative rings, the structure maps $\mathcal O_X(U)\to\mathcal P(U)$ form a morphism of presheaves of rings $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P$ (each $\rho_{UV}$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map), and $\iota:\mathcal F\to\mathcal P$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. (This is the presheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U))$ of Modules, Lemma 01CG, whose sheafification is Stacks' $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$; the Lemma's proof remarks that it may be more efficient to define $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ this way, which we do.)

source.place: Modules, Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior, line 3255) and Lemma 01CG (lemma-local-tensor-algebra, line 3297, with its proof)

proof.text: *Step 2 (definition of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ and $j_{\mathcal F}$).* By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) the presheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal P$ has a sheafification $\theta:\mathcal P\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal P^\#$ in sheaves of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $\sigma=\theta\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P):\mathcal O_X\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$, a morphism of sheaves of rings; so $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ is a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, an $\mathcal O_X$-module by $r\cdot b=\sigma(r)b$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\theta$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, in particular $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Put $j_{\mathcal F}=\theta\circ\iota:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map. For every open $U$, $\theta_U:\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U))\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map with $\theta_U\iota_U=j_{\mathcal F,U}$, hence by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property] it is *the* $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map extending $j_{\mathcal F,U}$ referred to in (b).

*Step 3 (the universal property (a) and functoriality).* Let $(\mathcal B,\tau)$ be a sheaf of commutative $\mathcal O_X$-algebras and $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal B$ $\mathcal O_X$-linear. Existence: for each open $U$, $\mathcal B(U)$ is a commutative $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra via $\tau_U$ and $u_U$ is $\mathcal O_X(U)$-linear, so there is a unique $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map $b_U:\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$ with $b_U\iota_U=u_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-universal-property]. For $V\subseteq U$, $b_V\rho_{UV}$ and $(\cdot)|_V\circ b_U$ are $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra maps $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(V)$ which agree on $\iota_U(s)$ (both give $u_V(s|_V)=u_U(s)|_V$), so they are equal; thus $b:\mathcal P\to\mathcal B$ is a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings with $b\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P)=\tau$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheafification-space-underlying-abelian](1) there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of rings $\tilde u:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)\to\mathcal B$ with $\tilde u\theta=b$; then $\tilde u\sigma=b\circ(\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal P)=\tau$, so $\tilde u$ is a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras, and $\tilde u j_{\mathcal F}=\tilde u\theta\iota=b\iota=u$. Uniqueness: if $\tilde u'$ is a morphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-algebras with $\tilde u'j_{\mathcal F}=u$, then $(\tilde u'\theta)_U$ is an $\mathcal O_X(U)$-algebra map $\mathcal P(U)\to\mathcal B(U)$ with $(\tilde u'\theta)_U\iota_U=u_U$, hence equals $b_U$; so $\tilde u'\theta=b=\tilde u\theta$ and $\tilde u'=\tilde u$ by the uniqueness in the sheafification property. Functoriality: for $\mathcal O_X$-linear $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ let $\operatorname{Sym}(v)$ be the map given by (a) for $u=j_{\mathcal F'}v$; by the uniqueness in (a), $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $\operatorname{Sym}(wv)=\operatorname{Sym}(w)\operatorname{Sym}(v)$ (both sides restrict along $j_{\mathcal F}$ to $j_{\mathcal F''}wv$). These two arguments use only that $\mathcal F,\mathcal F'$ are $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CG (the presheaf description); the universal property is not stated in Stacks and is written here by the agent from the sectionwise universal property of Sym (Algebra, Section 00DM) and that of sheafification

proof.text: *Step 4 (local setup on an affine open).* Fix an affine open $U\subseteq X$, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$, $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\mathcal P(U)$, and let $\iota_U:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ be the canonical open immersion with image $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]; via $\iota_U$ the opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the opens of $X$ contained in $U$, and the affine opens of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are the affine opens of $X$ contained in $U$ (an open subscheme isomorphic to an affine scheme). These form a basis of $U$ (every open of a scheme is covered by affine opens: standard opens $D(g)$ of affine opens are affine and form a basis, Schemes, Lemma 01I3 and Algebra, Lemma 00E0). Let $\mathcal S=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$ be the restriction of the $\mathcal O_X$-module $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ along $\iota_U$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], so $\mathcal S(V)=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(V)$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal S)=\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$ with its $R$-module structure through $\sigma_U$. Let $\widetilde A$ be the $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-module of the $R$-module $A$, with $\tau_V:A\to\widetilde A(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; it is quasi-coherent. The $R$-linear map $\theta_U:A\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal S)$ corresponds by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1) to a unique $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}R}$-linear $\alpha:\widetilde A\to\mathcal S$ with $\alpha_U\circ\tau_U=\theta_U$. For every affine open $V\subseteq U$, $\alpha_V\tau_V(a)=\alpha_V(\tau_U(a)|_V)=\alpha_U(\tau_U(a))|_V=\theta_U(a)|_V=\theta_V(\rho_{UV}(a))$ for $a\in A$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions: the mapping property of M~) and Section 01I6 (section-quasi-coherent-affine); route written by the agent

proof.text: *Step 5 (the sections over affine opens $V\subseteq U$, before sheafification).* Let $V\subseteq U$ be an affine open, $R_V=\mathcal O_X(V)$. (i) By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] for $\mathcal F$ (quasi-coherent) and $V\subseteq U$, the map $R_V\otimes_RM\to\mathcal F(V)$, $r\otimes m\mapsto r\,m|_V$, is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-base-change] (for $R\to R_V$) and this isomorphism, the $R_V$-algebra map $\lambda_V:R_V\otimes_RA\to\mathcal P(V)=\operatorname{Sym}_{R_V}(\mathcal F(V))$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,\rho_{UV}(a)$, is bijective: indeed $\rho_{UV}$ is the $R$-algebra map with $\iota_U(m)\mapsto\iota_V(m|_V)$, i.e. Sym of $M\to R_V\otimes_RM\cong\mathcal F(V)$, $m\mapsto 1\otimes m$, so $\lambda_V$ is the isomorphism of that node composed with $\operatorname{Sym}_{R_V}$ of an isomorphism. (ii) By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-affine-section-base-change] for the quasi-coherent $\widetilde A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ (affine opens $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$, $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\widetilde A)=A$ via $\tau_U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2)), the map $\beta_V:R_V\otimes_RA\to\widetilde A(V)$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,\tau_V(a)$, is bijective. (iii) $\alpha_V\beta_V=\theta_V\lambda_V$: both are $R_V$-linear ($\alpha$ is $\mathcal O$-linear, $\theta_V$ is an $R_V$-algebra map) and agree on $1\otimes a$ by the last formula of Step 4. (iv) For affine opens $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ and $c\in R_V\otimes_RA$, with $c'$ the image of $c$ under $R_V\otimes A\to R_W\otimes A$ (restriction on the first factor): $\lambda_W(c')=\rho_{VW}(\lambda_V(c))$ and $\beta_W(c')=\beta_V(c)|_W$, since on $r\otimes a$ both sides are $r|_W\rho_{UW}(a)$, resp. $r|_W\tau_W(a)$ (restrictions of $\mathcal P$ and $\widetilde A$ are semilinear and $\rho_{VW}\rho_{UV}=\rho_{UW}$, $\tau_V(a)|_W=\tau_W(a)$).

proof.text: *Step 7 (conclusions: quasi-coherence and (b)).* Every point of $X$ lies in an affine open $U$ (definition of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]), and by Step 6 $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)|_U\cong\widetilde A$ for the $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module $A=\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X(U)}(\mathcal F(U))$; so the underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module of $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For (b): for every affine open $U$, $\theta_U=\alpha_U\tau_U$ (Step 4) with $\tau_U$ bijective [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2) and $\alpha_U$ bijective (Step 6), so $\theta_U:\operatorname{Sym}_R(\mathcal F(U))\to\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)(U)$, which by Step 2 is the $R$-algebra map extending $j_{\mathcal F,U}$, is an isomorphism. (Stacks gets the quasi-coherence from Modules, Lemma 01CL, and the affine description from Schemes, Lemma 01I8(2), $\widetilde{\operatorname{Sym}^n(M)}\cong\operatorname{Sym}^n(\widetilde M)$, summed over $n$.)
